A probabilistic Turing machine (PTM) is a fixed multitape machine with two total ordinary transition tables. At each nonhalting transition a fresh independent fair bit selects the table. It is polynomial time if one fixed integer polynomial p bounds the number of transitions on every random branch on every input x by $p(|x|)$. This is a worst-case branch bound, using [[def-polynomial-time-verifier-and-reduction-interface]], not an expected-time bound.

For an input of length n, probabilities may be defined on the finite space $\Omega_n=\{0,1\}^{p(n)}$, giving every word mass $2^{-p(n)}$. A deterministic simulator uses bit j for transition j and ignores unused suffix bits after halting. Acceptance probability is the sum of masses of words giving acceptance. Independence has the finite-variable meaning of [[def-independence-of-finite-random-variables]]. The finite probability space is not itself storage charged to the machine.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

Let $t,s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$.

The function $t$ is **time-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

The function $s$ is **space-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_s$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts while using
$O(s(n))$ tape cells and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(s(n))$.

On this page, whenever a constructible bound is used to clock another machine,
we also require the evident size condition
$$ n\le t(n) $$
for large enough $n$, so that the budget is at least large enough to read an
input of length $n$.

derivations.claim: At the fixed input let $R=R(n)$ and let $A$ count accepting strings among the $2^R$ fair-bit strings, including unused suffixes after early halting; then $p=A/2^R$ by [F1]. The new machine first reads $R+2$ selector bits, rejecting only the all-zero selector. On every nonzero selector it simulates the original machine for at most $R$ steps using $R$ fresh bits, records its outcome, and consumes any unused suffix bits in a no-op state. On the zero selector it consumes all $R$ fresh bits and rejects. By [F3] this is a well-defined clocked procedure. There are exactly $2^{2R+2}$ equiprobable strings and exactly $(2^{R+2}-1)A$ accepting ones, so $p'=(1-2^{-(R+2)})p$.

If $p\le1/2$ then $p'<1/2$. If $p>1/2$, then $A\ge2^{R-1}+1$, so $p-1/2\ge2^{-R}$; because $p\le1$, $p'-1/2=(p-1/2)-p\,2^{-(R+2)}\ge2^{-R}-2^{-(R+2)}>0$. Thus strict majority is preserved and an original tie becomes a strict no-instance.

The new acceptance probability cannot equal one half: such equality would require the integer $A$ to equal $2^{2R+1}/(2^{R+2}-1)$, which is not an integer because its denominator is odd and greater than one. Since no tie remains, swapping accepting and rejecting labels makes the complement machine accept strictly above one half exactly on the original no-instances. The selector and padding add $2R+2$ transitions, so the overhead is $O(R(n))$.

$$ d:\mathbb B^*\to X\cup\{\mathtt{mal}\} $$

derivations.claim: Use the declared sequential multitape model, with its fixed finite alphabet, fixed number of heads, and heads initially at zero. Make halting states absorbing. In $T$ steps a head visits only positions $0,\ldots,T$, so each head address has $O(\log(T+2))$ bits. A candidate trace lists, for every time $t<T$, its state, head addresses and scanned/written symbols, together with the final state and addresses. Constant-table transition checks, binary increment/decrement/clamping checks, the initial state/address checks and final acceptance check have bounded-fan-in circuits of total size $O(T\log(T+2))$. Each table lookup has constant size because the simulated machine is fixed.

For a fixed deterministic machine in the derived basis profile and $T\ge n$, the deterministic instance of [F2] gives an exact index-only interpreter of time $T'=T\log^{O(1)}(T+2)$ whose actually used physical addresses and index words have $O(\log(T+2))$ bits. The description is fixed and its fair-bit tables agree, so no probabilistic choices affect this computation. The interpreter's source input, code and clock have total length $O(n+\log(T+2))$. Its explicit time bound can be rounded up to a fixed uniformly computable $T\log^c(T+2)$ clock. No sublinear-space preservation is needed for this formula construction.

For every tape and time create an access record containing tape ID, address, time, read symbol and written symbol, copied by wires from the trace. A read-only access has equal read/write symbols. Include initial records at time $-1$ for the at most $T+1$ relevant cells of the input tape, each with its actual input symbol as written symbol. Other tapes are initially blank. Use a validity bit and pad the records to a power of two by dummy records. Sort by (validity,tape,address,time), putting dummies last. Require each real record's read symbol to equal the preceding record's written symbol when the tape/address keys agree; at a first access to an address with no initial record require blank. Initial records need no read check. Thus the trace satisfies all these checks if and only if every reported read is the last symbol actually written to its addressed tape cell, or the correct initial symbol.

Here is the complete sorting construction used in step 2.1. Compare two $b$-bit keys lexicographically using the first unequal bit, realized by a prefix equality chain and Boolean gates; select both output records with multiplexers. This costs $O(b)$ gates. A bitonic merge of $2h$ records compares pairs at distance $h$, retaining smaller records in the first half and larger in the second, then recursively merges each half. To verify this, it suffices to consider Boolean keys: if sorting failed, applying a threshold between two inverted output keys commutes with every comparator and gives a Boolean failure. In a circular bitonic Boolean sequence the ones form one circular interval. The distance-$h$ comparisons therefore either remove all ones from the smaller half or all zeros from the larger half; both halves remain circular bitonic, and every smaller-half bit is at most every larger-half bit. Induction proves merge correctness. Sort two halves in opposite directions recursively, concatenate to form a bitonic sequence and merge. For $L$ padded records the merge uses $O(L\log L)$ comparisons and the sort uses $O(L\log^2L)$ comparisons. Here $L=O(T+1)$ and record width $b=O(\log(T+2))$, yielding $O(T\log^3(T+2))$ Boolean gates.

Memory consistency and the transition checks determine the trace uniquely from the input: induction on time first determines the scanned symbols from the earlier writes, and then the fixed deterministic transition determines the state, writes and next head addresses. The true trace passes all checks exactly when the original computation accepts. All sorting and checking gates are deterministic functions of the candidate trace. Introduce one variable for each gate output and constant-size clauses enforcing that gate's truth table; require the final checking conjunction to be true. For each input there is therefore exactly one satisfying assignment of all trace/gate variables when it accepts and none when it rejects. The number of clauses is the circuit size, and explicit binary variable names increase formula encoding length by at most $O(\log(T+2))$.

Fix the formula as the concatenation of fixed-width padded encodings of those local clauses. A gate has a tuple address consisting of module type, trace time or sorting round, wire number and bit/gate offset. Bitonic sorting pairs wire $i$ with $i\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}2^j$ in its round $(k,j)$; its direction is fixed by the relevant $k$th bit of $i$. In the recursive implementation this same tuple rule follows by the successive half merges described in step 3.1. Ripple comparisons and multiplexers have locally indexed predecessors. Thus one requested clause/variable-name bit is generated by $O(\operatorname{polylog}T)$ operations on $O(\log T)$-bit counters, storing only a fixed number of such counters. Decoding fixed-width clause offsets is integer arithmetic on $O(\log T)$ bits and costs polynomial time in $\log T$ even with school algorithms. Fix input-gate variables by unit clauses in one initial ordered block, with a common fixed clause-slot width and the clause for $x_i$ in slot $i$. Only this block contains actual $x$ symbols; all other clauses refer to variable names. Unfixed $y$ symbols remain input variables. For isolated bit generation, the bit generator uses the declared direct access to the indicated input bit. For sequential consumers, a unit move of the formula-input head changes the required source-input position by at most one inside this block; outside it park the source head at the nearest endpoint. This monotone address map charges all source-head motion to formula-head motion plus initial setup, so sequential on-demand generation uses polynomial-logarithmic overhead per formula-input transition and $O(\log T)$ workspace without uncharged random access. This proves logarithmic workspace and polylogarithmic output-bit time for the sequential construction; the separate derived-basis extension follows below.

Apply step 1.1 and step 2.1 and step 3.1 and step 4.1 and step 5.1 to a trace of this bounded-address interpreter, with one addition: each fixed native index tape is represented by its $O(\log T)$-bit accumulating value and length, updated by shift-and-append on an emitted bit and reset on use. A jump's next head address must equal that accumulated value. All addresses, states, index prefixes and counters use $O(\log T)$ bits, and the fixed number of heads contributes only a constant factor. Every prime $p$ admits a primitive root modulo $p$.

For $m,w\ge1$, the exact sum of $m$ nonnegative $w$-bit integers has constant-depth polynomial-size circuits over AND, OR, NOT and MAJ, with $w+\lceil\log_2m\rceil$ output bits. The circuits are DLOGTIME-uniform under the following explicit array convention: the input bit $x_{i,j}$ has tuple address $(i,j)$; array dimensions and gate-coordinate domains may be padded to powers of two, with padded inputs zero. Gate addresses use a fixed number of binary coordinate fields, and the uniformity machine receives the binary dimensions and gate addresses. Equivalently, the input is a bit matrix with both dimensions padded to powers of two. Constants and output truncation are included in the family. derivations.claim: A function of a fixed number of short arguments has polynomially many argument tuples. If its table is logspace-computable, realize each output bit by an OR of equality conjunctions over the tuples yielding one. This is a constant-depth polynomial-size logspace-uniform Boolean lookup circuit. Short addition, multiplication, reduction, inverses modulo a prime, and the table $(a,e,p)\mapsto a^e\bmod p$ have this property. For the power table, use repeated squaring with a constant number of short residues and a short exponent counter; short multiplication uses grade-school arithmetic in logarithmic space. Find an inverse by trying every short candidate, and test primality by trial division. Enumerate the $j$-th prime by a counter and these primality tests whenever $j$ and that prime are polynomially bounded. We may also add polynomially many polynomial-width words by [F3], whose uniformity is stronger than required here.

For a fixed short prime $p>2$, [F2] gives a generator $g$ of the nonzero residues. Find the least such $g$ by testing all candidates and all exponents below $p-1$ with step 1.1. The tables $a\mapsto\ell(a)$, where $g^{\ell(a)}\equiv a\pmod p$ and $0\le\ell(a)<p-1$, and $(g,e,p)\mapsto g^e\bmod p$ are logspace-computable by enumeration and modular powering with a constant number of short counters. For nonzero inputs $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ with polynomially bounded $d$, their product modulo $p$ is $g^{\sum_i\ell(a_i)}\bmod p$. The exponent sum is polynomially bounded, so compute it with [F3] and use a short power lookup. If any input is zero, select zero instead. For $p=2$, the product is one exactly when all inputs are one. This gives iterated multiplication in any fixed polynomial-size residue basis in logspace-uniform constant depth. It uses only short tables and addition, without assuming binary iterated multiplication.

Convert a long word $X=\sum_j x_j2^j$ to residues by computing $x_j(2^j\bmod p)$ for each bit position and modulus, summing these short contributions with [F3], and reducing the result modulo $p$ by step 1.1. The sum is polynomially bounded in $N$, because its number of contributions and $p$ are. Each constant $2^j\bmod p$ is logspace-computable. Thus binary-to-residue conversion has the required circuit bounds; for $X$ outside the basis range, its vector represents its remainder in that range.

There are $2^P+(A-B)$ accepting choice strings out of $2^{P+1}$, so the transcript-validity language $C=\{h>0\}$ has a matching-profile quasilinear probabilistic decider. Normalize the original outer oracle machine by [F1] before this construction. Keep its original fixed-length fair-bit string $p$ separate from a guessed fixed-length transcript record $t$, whose unused suffix is canonically zero. Simulate the original machine on $p$ using the proposed answers in $t$, and record whether its queries match the listed queries and its final outcome accepts. Make a single final query to $C$ containing the record and this flag; extend $C$ to reject whenever the flag fails. There is exactly one correct answer/rank-witness record for each $p$ by step 1.2. Consequently exactly one $t$ gives a YES query when the original path accepts and none do when it rejects. The number of successful pairs $(p,t)$ is the original accepting-path count. Fix the original fair string $p$, and put $H=|t|$, $k=|z|$. Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

Let $\mathbb B:=\{0,1\}$. A **binary encoding** of a set $X$ is an injective
function
$$ e:X\to\mathbb B^* $$
([[def-function]], [[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]).

Fix a symbol $\mathtt{mal}$ not belonging to $X$. A **total decoder** for $e$
is a function
$$ d:\mathbb B^*\to X\cup\{\mathtt{mal}\} $$
such that
$$ d(e(x))=x\quad(x\in X),\qquad d(w)=\mathtt{mal}\quad(w\notin e[X]). $$
Thus $\mathtt{mal}$ is exactly the output on malformed codes, and the decoder
is defined on every binary word, not only on words in the image of $e$.

The encoding $e$ is **effective** when such a total decoder is specified.

The encoding is **prefix-free** when no codeword is a proper prefix of another:
there do not exist distinct $x,y\in X$ and a nonempty binary word $u$ with
$e(y)=e(x)u$.

Let $t,s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$.

The function $t$ is **time-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

The function $s$ is **space-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_s$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts while using
$O(s(n))$ tape cells and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(s(n))$.

On this page, whenever a constructible bound is used to clock another machine,
we also require the evident size condition
$$ n\le t(n) $$
for large enough $n$, so that the budget is at least large enough to read an
input of length $n$.

derivations.claim: Specify the syntax rather than appealing to an arbitrary effective code. Use canonical binary numeric fields, each encoded as $1^{|w|}0w$, and encode a tuple of $a$ such fields by $1^a0$ followed by their encodings. Supply two complete transition tables, one for each fair-bit value. The virtual input tape is read-only, each work tape is initially blank, and each head starts at cell zero with clamped left motion. The finite input alphabet is the two binary input symbols, distinguished from blank. A header lists the tape count $k$, alphabet size $r$, state count $m$, start and two distinct halting states; the two tables list every nonhalting state/scanned-symbol tuple in lexicographic order, each with its next state, written symbols, and local moves or stationary requests. For the read-only tape require its written symbol to equal the scanned symbol. All integers use canonical binary numerals, all blocks carry unary length headers, and the number of blocks is unary-prefixed. Include explicit table delimiters and a profile tag. This is prefix-free, includes each finite machine of the chosen numeric form, and has a total decoder. If the start state is nonhalting, a complete table contains at least one row with $k$ symbol/move fields and contains all nonhalting states and scanned symbols, giving $k\le L$, $r\le L+3$ and $m\le L+3$. An initially halting machine will instead be handled without per-tape initialization by an early return after validation. Each stored integer has at most $L$ bits even without these sharper bounds.

For this erased-index interpreter put $H=n+b+L+2$, $s=\lceil\log_2 H\rceil$ and $B=2^s$, so $B>n$ and $B>b$. Use the explicit unary-length tuple syntax from the sequential candidate, now adding finite head labels, the source index-tape labels, a profile tag, index-output actions and native jump actions to each transition row. A row specifies all source actions, and the complete table explicitly includes every state/scanned-symbol/bit case. For nonhalting start states, at least one such row exists, so the number $h$ of source heads and index tapes, every alphabet width, and each instruction-record width are bounded by a fixed polynomial in $L$. Initially halting machines use that early return. The source's one binary work tape is included as a special case; any allowed finite additional tapes receive tape labels. Parse and validate by capped expected-count arithmetic without expanding an asserted table; this takes $L^{O(1)}$ time. State and scanned-symbol lookup by repeated scans of the saved table costs $L^{O(1)}$ per source transition. The fixed physical interpreter never acquires a new head or an alphabet depending on $e$.

Parse and check the actual blocks without expanding a claimed table. Count the actual rows first; compute expected products and powers by binary arithmetic capped one above that actual count, rejecting excess, invalid ranges, missing rows or extra data. If there are no nonhalting states, the expected row count is zero without computing a power or iterating over tape/head labels. Check each actual row's arity against the binary header by counting its actual fields, never by a loop of header-specified length. This bounds all valid and invalid code processing by a polynomial in $L$: the operands, counters and scans have length $O(L)$, there are $O(L)$ actual blocks, and every product/exponent loop is capped or uses at most $L$ exponent bits. Ordinary repeated scans and school arithmetic suffice, for example in $O(L^6)$ time and $O(L^2)$ space. After validation, if the start state is halting, report that outcome immediately, even for $b=0$, without allocating or initializing per-tape or per-head structures. Otherwise the parameter bounds of steps 1.1 and 1.2 apply to all following phases. Preserve a decoded table of length $O(L^2)$, runtime parameters and fixed-width symbol/state codes of width at most $L+O(1)$. Copy $x$ to a sequential archive and read/copy the clock in $O(n+\log(b+2))$ time. All subsequent routines use fixed physical tape counts and fixed alphabets; variable-size data remain on tapes.

For each source index tape reserve a separate contiguous region of $b+1$ binary cells, with its current length stored in metadata. Reserve these regions by arithmetic base offsets before the dictionary heap; reservation moves no head through the regions and requires no initialization sweep. A source index emits at most one bit per source transition, so its live word always fits. Appending a source bit writes at its region's base plus current length and increments that length. Use/reset sets the length to zero; future emission overwrites old bits, and reading only the current prefix ignores the discarded suffix. Interleaved emission onto different source indexes therefore never interleaves their physical words. Since at most $h$ bits are emitted per source transition, the sum $W$ of lengths of all words consumed at jumps, plus lengths still live at expiry, satisfies $W\le h b$, up to a harmless fixed-format constant. A jump using one word for several source heads in the same transition multiplies this accounting by at most $h$, still a polynomial in $L$. Reading, copying or canonicalizing each consumed word once, or a fixed number of times per affected head, therefore has total length $L^{O(1)}b$. The reserved regions' total extent is $O(h(b+1))$, consistent with later maximum-address bounds. This charged fresh-writing invariant is exactly what fails for the old nonerasing delimited-head model.

Split each numerical source head address $a$ uniquely as $a=PB+r$, where $0\le r<B$. Call $P$ its block prefix and $r$ its short offset. Store the short offset in $s$ bits. Maintain a global prefix dictionary assigning one compact integer block ID to each registered numerical prefix. A dictionary key for $P$ is the prefix-free word $1^{|w|}0w$, where $w$ is the canonical binary numeral of $P$, including $w=0$ at zero. Use a literal binary trie: each node has two child pointers, an optional terminal block ID and its fixed metadata. Reading/inserting a key follows or creates one node per bit. Numerical equality of prefixes is equality of their canonical words, hence exactly equality of terminal nodes. No balancing, probabilistic hashing, numerical unit-cost large integers or unspecified dictionary theorem is required. Include a tape label in this key when more than one virtual work tape is allowed.

For each virtual tape, store its scanned cell as a centre and the cells on either side as two ordered stacks, nearest cell first. At level $i$, put $h_i=2^i$; each side has capacity $2h_i$, occupancy $0,h_i$ or $2h_i$, and complementary occupancies summing to $2h_i$. Initially each side has occupancy $h_i$ at every level; the right stack holds the input suffix on the input tape and blanks elsewhere, and all left stacks are blank. Each record has an immutable origin bit, one exactly for source cell zero; it moves with the symbol record. Genuine records are packed at the near end of each zone, and concatenating zones while ignoring holes gives the stack. Each physical slot has $k$ delimited virtual fields, each of width at most $L+O(1)$, containing a symbol and an immutable origin bit, or a hole. Store the $k$ centre fields and the $k$ three-valued occupancy flags explicitly. A slot therefore has width $O(L^2)$; this uses no alphabet depending on $e$ and no additional physical tape for each virtual tape. A stationary move changes only the centre symbol. At the left origin a requested left move also changes only that symbol. For the input tape suppress writes. These modifications preserve the same stack and origin invariants.

On a source head's jump, read the consumed address word, discard leading zeros and split off its final $s$ bits as $r$, padding on the left with zeros if the word has fewer than $s$ bits. The remaining canonical prefix is $P$, or zero. Form canonical $P-1$ when $P>0$, $P$ and $P+1$ by ordinary binary scans; forming all three costs $O(A+s)$ for address-word length $A$. Register them in the prefix trie. Record their three compact IDs as a private cache for this head, and record that the current block is the middle one. Use a special clamped boundary marker instead of a negative block when $P=0$. Initialize each source head at address zero with this same cache for zero and one. If several source heads jump to the same address, their numerical prefixes receive the same global IDs. The total number of prefix-trie nodes is at most the total length of all registered keys, hence at most $L^{O(1)}(b+1)$: for each jump, all three prefix keys have length $O(A+1)$, and step 2.2 charges their summed lengths. Duplicated registrations only decrease the node count. Tape-label overhead adds at most $L^{O(1)}$ bits per jump.

Implement a move to the right by first writing the old centre $c$ and choosing the least $i$ with a nonempty right zone. All lower right zones are empty and their left partners full. Remove the first $h_i$ records of right zone $i$: the first becomes the new centre, and the remaining $h_i-1=\sum_{j<i}h_j$ fill the lower right zones in order, $h_j$ per zone. Right occupancy at level $i$ decreases by $h_i$. Prepend $c$ to the concatenation of the lower left zones. The resulting $1+2\sum_{j<i}h_j=2h_i-1$ records split into a first list of length $h_i-1$, distributed in order half-full among the lower left zones, and a remaining list of length $h_i$, prepended to left zone $i$. Its previous occupancy was zero or $h_i$, so no capacity is exceeded. Both stacks keep their order, complementary occupancies at level $i$ are preserved, and every lower zone becomes half-full. For $i=0$ these instructions simply exchange a stack record with the centre and push the old centre on the other stack. A left move interchanges left and right; at the origin it only writes the centre. Untouched higher zones are half-full, so a source zone always exists. Thus every operation preserves the representation and performs exactly the prescribed source move.

Between two jumps of this head, its address changes by at most $b$ in total absolute distance from its most recent jump address, since every local move changes it by at most one and there are at most $b$ source transitions altogether. As $B>b$, every intervening address belongs to one of the three blocks $P-1,P,P+1$ cached at that jump. A local move updates the $s$-bit offset; overflow/underflow switches to the appropriate adjacent cached ID and wraps the offset. Store the current cache position as one of three finite values. Even if the head crosses the same block boundary many times, the existing IDs are reused, with no re-reading or arithmetic on long prefixes. From the lower cached block it cannot cross to an uncached lower block, and from the upper cached block it cannot cross to an uncached upper block: either would require more than $B$ local moves since the jump. Clamp a left move at numerical zero. Thus the pair (current block ID, short offset) is always an exact address representation, with $O(\log H+\log L)$ bits after accounting for the polynomial number of trie nodes.

Make the scan algorithms uniform as follows. To process virtual field $j$, keep a unary field index of length at most $L$; at each slot count through the delimited fields, copy or replace just field $j$, and copy the other fields unchanged. A full slot, its index operations, and returning a scratch head across the bounded parameter records cost at most $O(L^4)$. The same bound covers building one fresh slot by copying the saved width and tape-count templates. Midpoint/end markers specify half-zones, so the scans need no growing arithmetic per record. Copying the selected genuine field records to scratch, distributing the prescribed lists, restoring holes and flags, and returning the physical heads use a fixed number of prefix scans for step 4.1; at level $i$ they traverse $O(2^i)$ slots. Endpoint and optional level-label overhead is also $O(2^i)$, since the sum of the binary level-label lengths through $i$ is $O(2^i)$. Thus the work for a level-$i$ event on one virtual tape is at most $C_1L^6 2^i$, uniformly in $e,i$. This deliberately generous bound includes scans to find the least nonempty source zone, scratch copying, occupancy changes and allocating new levels by doubling the preceding unary capacity marker. Each operation is a scan, a finite-width copy, or an index operation of length at most $O(L)$; no unit-cost random memory operation is being assumed.

The event count is independent of field width. Fix a virtual tape and $i\ge1$. Its right occupancy below level $i$ starts at $H_i=2^i-1$. Each event at level at least $i$ resets it to $H_i$; a lower-level positive or negative move changes it by minus or plus one, and a stationary or clamped move leaves it fixed. An event at level at least $i$ requires the appropriate lower stack empty, hence occupancy zero or $2H_i$ immediately beforehand. It therefore requires at least $H_i$ preceding lower-level moves and then its triggering transition. Among $b$ simulated transitions there are at most $\lfloor b/2^i\rfloor$ such events, including the first. Level zero has at most $b$ events, and no level with $2^i>b$ is reached. The redistribution in step 4.1 resets all lower zones even when its level is strictly larger than $i$; successive operations on different virtual tapes do not change each other's fields.

Maintain a second literal binary trie for virtual work cells, keyed by the compact block ID and the $s$-bit offset, with explicit length delimiters (and virtual tape label if needed). The key length is $O(\log H+\log L)$. Every terminal stores the virtual symbol, initially zero/blank on first lookup. Each source transition touches at most $h$ virtual cells, so there are at most $h(b+1)$ terminal keys and $L^{O(1)}(b+1)\log H$ nodes in this trie. All keys with the same virtual cell get the same terminal, regardless of which source head or which jump registered that prefix. Source work-tape collisions can therefore be detected by comparing these compact address pairs for all relevant heads, in $L^{O(1)}\log H$ work per transition. Omit precisely the operations declared undefined by the source's collision convention. Read all source scanned symbols and save all source instructions before any virtual write or move.

Initially retain the input archive at position one and initialize only the centres. On first allocating level $i$, fill the first virtual tape's untouched right half from the next $h_i$ archive symbols, then blanks after exhaustion; initialize the other virtual fields with blank and unoccupied halves with holes. Levels are allocated in increasing order, and lower operations do not alter that untouched suffix, so every archive symbol is consumed at most once. A new level uses only the work charged to the event reaching it. Initially right zone $i$ represents source positions $2^i,\ldots,2^{i+1}-1$; hence the archive is exactly at the next untouched interval. Slot creation and symbol coding are charged by step 5.1. Thus no full $n\log n$ distribution pass is hidden in initialization.

Before each virtual transition, test the saved state, then test expiry. If still nonhalting with positive countdown, consume one fresh fair bit to choose the corresponding decoded table. Deterministically scan its rows and compare the source state/scanned-symbol tuple with the saved state and centres, copying the unique instructions into scratch. At most $O(L)$ rows and $O(L^2)$ saved fields are involved; repeated full scans and resets take $O(L^6)$ per transition. Save all instructions before applying any virtual write/move, process the $k$ buffer operations in order, then update the state and decrement the binary countdown. Test the new halting state before the next expiry test, so a halt on transition $b$ is reported. A whole countdown scan costs $O(\log(b+2))$ per virtual transition. At $b=0$ the nonhalting initial configuration expires immediately.

Treat read-only input separately. Since $n<B$, an input-head address is in range only if its block prefix is zero and its short offset is an input position. The global trie has the distinguished ID for zero, so this is a comparison of compact IDs followed by comparison of $s$-bit integers. On an in-range address issue a native input query with the original short address, or its fixed encoding-offset translation if the physical interpreter input is a paired encoding of $(e,x,b)$. This translation has $O(\log H)$ bits. On an out-of-range address return the source's prescribed blank. The same compact head representation implements local input moves and jumps. The original input is never expanded into the work-cell trie.

Store the two tries, the reserved source index-word regions, finite-program records, per-head caches, short counters and scratch on allocated regions of the interpreter's single binary classical work tape. Encode record delimiters and symbols by constant-length binary blocks. Long key/input-word arrays have total length $L^{O(1)}(b+1)$; trie nodes and other records have length $L^{O(1)}\log H$. The cell trie has $L^{O(1)}(b+1)\log H$ nodes by step 5.3. Consequently every physical location used is below $L^{O(1)}(b+1)\log^{O(1)}H$, and every pointer has $O(\log H+\log L)$ bits. No source's enormous numerical address is used as a physical memory location. Reserve the polynomially sized source-program/scratch region and the $O(h(b+1))$ source-index regions by arithmetic offsets, then use a global high-water counter to append-allocate the dictionary heap and saved long keys. This reserves address intervals without writing their unused cells.

Buffer correctness from step 4.1 and the saved-instructions ordering imply by induction that after each virtual transition the interpreter stores the exact virtual configuration prescribed by the consumed bits. Although the physical probabilistic machine receives a bit at every physical transition, ignore all of them except at the designated virtual-choice operation. Conditional on every past consumed bit and the corresponding completed deterministic simulation, the next designated bit is still unbiased and independent: its location depends only on previous bits, and disjoint future coordinates of a finite independent-bit string have the prescribed fair conditional law. Equivalently, for each fixed virtual choice prefix of length $j$, induction on its successive designated choice operations gives probability $2^{-j}$; ignored physical bits have total conditional probability one. Terminal virtual prefixes are disjoint. Summing their masses proves exact agreement of acceptance/rejection/timeout probabilities, including branch-dependent halt times.

Summing step 5.1 using step 5.2, first for each tape and then over $k\le L$, bounds total buffer and lazy-allocation work by $$ C_2L^7\left(b+\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor\log_2 b\rfloor}2^i\lfloor b/2^i\rfloor\right)\le C_2L^7 b(1+\lfloor\log_2 b\rfloor) $$ when $b\ge1$. Add polynomial code processing, the $O(n)$ input archive scan, transition lookup, and the binary-clock work. The physical heads move locally by at most one cell per transition, as required by the sequential profile. Enlarging the absolute exponent to $d=8$ and the constant covers all contributions, the binary-clock input length, and $b=0$. This proves the general displayed bound.

Choose one pointer width $q=K(s+\lceil\log_2 L\rceil+1)$ at initialization, for an absolute constant $K$ exceeding all fixed exponents in step 6.4. The separation proof uses the explicit uniform interpreters [[lem-qc-uniform-probabilistic-clocked-simulation]] and [[lem-qc-basis-query-time-normalization]].

For constants $\alpha>1$ and $0<\beta<1$ there is a finite integer $\tau(\alpha,\beta)$ such that $\mathrm{PrTISP}_P(n^\alpha,n^{1-\beta})\subseteq\mathrm{LCH}_{P,\tau}$ for either fixed profile $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$. The basis profile is the explicitly derived full-basis comparison, with native queries and charged operand endpoints.

For either fixed profile $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, every $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}$ language reduces to MajSAT, and every $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,2}$ language reduces to MajMajSAT, with output length n log^O(1)n and each output bit computable in log^O(1)n time and O(log n) space, in the explicit input/machine/formula encodings. Basis means the derived full-basis restriction; isolated output-bit generation has direct source-input bit access, and the reduction also admits sequential on-demand generation with polylogarithmic overhead per formula-head transition.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

For an explicitly coded machine in the derived full classical basis profile, input $x$ of length $n$, and external transition clock $b\ge n$, there is a fixed finite-head index-only erased-index interpreter reproducing exact acceptance, rejection and timeout probabilities. Writing $L=|e|+1$ for source description length, its time and maximum physical work-access address are bounded by
$$C L^d\bigl(n+(b+1)\log^d(n+b+L+2)\bigr)$$
for absolute constants $C,d$. In particular, logarithmic descriptions and each fixed polynomial clock $T(n)\ge n$ have $O(T(n)\,\mathrm{polylog}(n+2))$ overhead, including clock construction. This is a time-only normalization; it does not preserve a smaller original source space bound and makes no general equivalence claim for clocks below input length.

Let $x$ have length $n$, and let $y(x)$ have known length $N\le(n+2)^K$. Suppose its zero-based bit $y_i(x)$ can be generated deterministically in $\log^{O(1)}(n+2)$ time and $O(\log(n+2))$ work cells, with ordinary direct indexed access to $x$. Fix a classical derived-basis machine whose run on $y(x)$ takes at most a known polynomial clock $T\le(n+2)^K$ and whose work operands, including native query endpoints, all lie below a known power of two $M\le(n+2)^K$. The dimensions and clocks have polylogarithmic-time/logspace binary generators. There is an index-only erased-index simulation on $x$ with identical branch outcomes and probabilities, time $O((n+T+1)\log^{O(1)}(n+2))$, and work-access extent $O(M+\log(n+2))$. The simulated machine has fixed finite head and tape counts; its constants may depend on that machine, the generators and $K$. This does not assert a sublinear-time simulation or normalization of unrestricted work addresses.

In the basis profile use [F6] to simulate both ordinary reads and native basis queries on this generated formula in time $O((n+N+N^d+1)\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ and space $O(M+\log n)$. In the sequential profile [F3]'s ordered source-constant block, or a logarithmic virtual-input-position counter, gives at most the same overhead for each local input move without changing work records. The strict margins $a>\max(d,1)$ and $\eta<\eta_1$ bound these resources by $O(n^a)$ and $O(n^{1-\eta})$. Hence $\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)\subseteq\mathrm{PrTISP}_P(n^a,n^{1-\eta})$.

Choose rational $1<b<B$ with $B(1-\eta)<1$, put $\beta=1-B(1-\eta)>0$, and choose rational $A>Ba$. For any $\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n^b)$ language, its self-delimited padded version at length $m=\Theta(n^B)$ has a linear-time decider. In the basis profile apply [F5] to the original fixed decider, then translate its short indices to the original-input portion of the actual padded word; the cost $n^b\mathrm{polylog}\,n$ fits $O(m)$ because $b<B$. Sequential simulation is no slower. Apply step 1.1 to that padded language. On the original word, its resulting time/space decider sees a generated input of length $m$. For the basis profile [F6] simulates this virtual padded input with a known work bound $M=O(m^{1-\eta})$ rounded to a power of two; its delimiter and zero bits have polylogarithmic-time/logspace generators. Thus $\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n^b)\subseteq\mathrm{PrTISP}_P(n^A,n^{1-\beta})\subseteq\mathrm{LCH}_{P,\tau}$ by [F2] for a fixed finite $\tau$. Increase $\tau$ to at least two if necessary.

Choose rational constants $1<c<\rho<\delta<b^{1/(\tau-1)}$ and suppose $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ has a fixed $\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n^c)$ decider. Let the reduction in [F3] map an $n$-bit input to a formula $y=R(x)$ of length $N=O(n\log^k(n+2))$ for some fixed $k$, with the stated direct bit generator. If $P=\mathrm{seq}$, supply this formula on demand using [F3]'s sequential streaming guarantee; the decider then takes $O(N^c\mathrm{polylog}\,n)=O(n^c\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time. If $P=\mathrm{basis}$, the bit generator alone does not justify composition with a time-only decider that can issue long block queries. Choose a constructible clock $T=\lceil K_0(N+2)^c\rceil\ge N$ and apply [F5] to the decider's fixed explicit code. The resulting exact index-only interpreter has time and physical work-access extent bounded by a constructible $T'=O(N^c\mathrm{polylog}\,N)$. Choose a power-of-two majorant $M_n=2^{\lceil K_1\log_2(n+2)\rceil}$ with fixed $K_1$ large enough that $T'\le M_n\le(n+2)^{K_1+1}$. The normalized index-only interpreter is a special case of the basis machine's head-access operations, with no native block query left; apply [F6] to its run on the generated formula $R(x)$. The formula length, bit generator, clock and address majorant satisfy [F6]'s hypotheses, so the exact simulation takes $O((n+T'+1)\log^{O(1)}(n+2))=O(n^c\log^{O(1)}n)$ time. Thus in either profile $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,2}\subseteq\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n^\rho)$, with the strict exponent margin absorbing the reduction, normalization and generated-input overheads.

We prove the stronger induction assertion that for every $j\ge2$ there is a rational $e'_j<\delta^{j-1}$ with $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}\subseteq\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n^{e'_j})$. The base is $e'_2=\rho$. This padded language is in $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}$: verify its format in $O(m)$ time and run the $B$ decider on the logical input $q$. For $P=\mathrm{basis}$, first apply [F5] to the fixed $B$ decider on its actual $|q|$-bit input using the constructible clock $T_q=\lceil K_2(|q|+2)^{e'_j}\rceil\ge |q|$. The normalized interpreter's index-only input reads are redirected to the encoded $q$ substring, returning the original blank or zero answer for addresses outside that substring; offsetting and saturating the emitted input indices is charged within the normalization bound. Its run takes $O(|q|^{e'_j}\mathrm{polylog}\,|q|)=O(m)$ because $e'_j<e$. The sequential case reads the same encoded substring by local input moves within the same bound. Hence the padded language belongs to $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}$. The original linear-time oracle machine for $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}$ makes queries whose total lengths are $O(n)$. For $P=\mathrm{seq}$, use that machine directly on the logical input $x$. For $P=\mathrm{basis}$, apply [F5] to its fixed code with a constructible clock $K_4(n+2)\ge n$; [F4] permits forwarding its exact completed oracle queries and answers. The resulting index-only simulation takes $O(n\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time. Use a self-delimited padded input with the length and $x$ available in a designated prefix. The padded-language machine checks that encoding in $O(m)$ time; the index-only simulation redirects each logical input read to the encoded $x$ substring and returns the original blank/zero answer outside it. This offset handling is charged to the emitted input-index bits. Replace each query $q$ by its padded version of length $\Theta((|q|+2)^e)$. The sum of these query lengths is $O(\sum_q(|q|+2)^e)=O(n^e)$ because the original query lengths and query count sum to $O(n)$. Padding counters and query writes have the same total bound, so the padded outer language is decided in $O(m)$ time with oracle $B_e\in\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}$ and hence lies in $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,2}$.

Apply the $m^\rho$ time decider from step 3.1 to that padded outer language, whose input is $y=\operatorname{pad}_e(x)$ of length $m=\Theta((n+2)^e)$. In the basis profile its block queries may again use long address blocks, so normalize this decider with [F5] at the constructible clock $T_m=\lceil K_3(m+2)^\rho\rceil\ge m$. Its exact index-only interpreter has time and physical work-access extent bounded by a constructible $T'_m=O(m^\rho\mathrm{polylog}\,m)$. The bits of $y$ are generated from $x$ by the self-delimited prefix and zero-padding map in polylogarithmic time and logarithmic space; its padding length, the clocks, and the address majorants have polylog-time/logspace binary generators. Since $T'_m$ is polynomial in $n$, choose a constructible power-of-two address majorant $M_n=2^{\lceil K\log_2(n+2)\rceil}\le(n+2)^{K+1}$ and apply [F6] to simulate the normalized run on this generated input. The resulting time is $O((n+T'_m+1)\log^{O(1)}(n+2))=O(n^{e\rho}\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$. In the sequential profile, supply the same padded bits on demand to the sequential decider with at most polylogarithmic overhead per input transition. Choose rational $e'_{j+1}$ strictly between $e\rho$ and $e\delta=\delta^j$; the strict margin absorbs all polylogarithmic factors. Steps 2.1 and 4.1–5.1 give $\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n^b)\subseteq\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n^{\delta^{\tau-1}})$ although $\delta^{\tau-1}<b$. Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call. Inverse availability and query or gate charges are also recorded separately from controlled forward access. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $D$ be a finite ordered quantum register and let $A$ be an ordered register of $k\ge0$ ancilla qubits, with Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_D$ and $\mathcal H_A$. Write $|0_A\rangle=|0^k\rangle$, including $|0_A\rangle=1$ when $k=0$. Let $U$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$ and let $V$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D$.

The register $A$ is a **clean ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when
$$
U(|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle
$$
for every vector $|\psi\rangle_D$. Thus the data operation is independent of the input vector and all clean wires return exactly to zero.

The register $A$ is a **dirty ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when the operator identity $U=V\otimes I_A$ holds on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$. Equivalently, every product input $|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$ is mapped to $V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$, with the same $V$ for every data and ancilla vector. This requires exact restoration of an arbitrary, initially unknown ancilla state and forbids residual data–ancilla correlation.

These are exact contracts for the complete subroutine. A temporary intermediate alteration of an ancilla is permitted if the full unitary satisfies the stated identity.

Use the **published VMW model** from Van Melkebeek and Watson, Theory of Computing 8 (2012), §2.3.1–2.3.2. It has three semi-infinite tapes: read-only binary input followed by blanks; a zero-initialized classical binary work tape; and a zero-initialized quantum work tape. There are a fixed finite number of heads, possibly several per tape. Each classical control state has an associated local classical function and local quantum operation, applied jointly to the cells under the respective work heads. The next control state and head movements depend on the current state, the input/classical symbols scanned at the beginning of the transition, and that transition's measurement outcome, if any. Earlier outcomes can influence later operations through the control state. These choices do not depend on the quantum basis path. A quantum operation is a unitary on the cells under the quantum heads or a single-qubit computational-basis measurement.

Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to a precomputed classical address. Addresses are written on special one-way sequential-access write-only index tapes and those tapes are erased after every use; all index-bit writing is charged to ordinary transitions. Coherent input access may apply $|i,b\rangle\mapsto|i,b\mathbin\oplus x_i\rangle$ to a contiguous quantum-work block, with out-of-range input bit zero. The endpoint convention is $[l,r]$: the MSB-first address occupies $[l,r)$ and the answer is cell $r$; use input indices $1,\ldots,n$, $x_0=0$, empty address zero, and omit a reversed-endpoint query. Its two endpoint addresses are likewise supplied on these erased index tapes. The coherent query itself costs one transition. The classical input tape's out-of-range cells are blank. These two output conventions are distinct and fixed by the source. If colliding work heads make an operation undefined, omit the operation on that work tape.

Input cells and the separate index tapes are not counted in the maximum-workhead-address space measure. Space is the maximum address of any work operand: ordinary classical/quantum head visits and the highest endpoint of every native query block are all charged; time and space maximize over every branch, including branches of probability zero. For each fixed unitary matrix entry, real and imaginary parts have deterministic approximators computing precision $p$ in time polynomial in $p$. This permits polylogarithmic time and workspace at precision $p=O(\log t)$; it does not assert linear-space approximators for arbitrary entries.

For a promise problem $(Y,N)$, $\mathrm{BQTISP}(t,s)$ means such a machine takes $O(t)$ transitions and maximum work address $O(s)$ on every branch, accepts $Y$ with probability at least $2/3$, and accepts $N$ with probability at most $1/3$. No acceptance guarantee is required off the promise; the resource bounds remain worst-case. $\mathrm{BQTIME}(t)$ omits the space bound. Its classical comparison classes are the explicitly derived full-basis comparison classes $\mathrm{PrTIME}_{\mathrm{basis}}$ and $\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\mathrm{basis}}$ in [[def-qc-unbounded-error-time-space-counting-model]]. They permit a fixed finite product of classical basis tapes with the same native input-query operation. No generic inclusion into the narrower erased-index head-access-only class is assumed.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

ordered computational basis are

$$H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\omega\end{pmatrix},\qquad T^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\omega^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$

is control and the second target. A circuit is a finite chronological word of
these gates at stated wire positions; its matrix is the product with later
gates on the left. No extra wire or controlled-$T$ operation is implicit.

The scalar phase $\omega I$ is an allowed Clifford phase in the one-qubit
matrix-word convention. Its scalar factor is retained in exact matrix products;
the convention that an overall scalar does not affect a resource count is
stated separately from matrix equality. It does not grant a controlled-$T$

The exact one-qubit H/T algebra is generated by $H,T,T^\dagger$; $S$ and $Z$
are aliases for the displayed powers. The distinction between exact matrix
