Let $t,s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$.

The function $t$ is **time-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_t$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts within
$O(t(n))$ steps and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(t(n))$.

The function $s$ is **space-constructible** when there exists a deterministic
machine $C_s$ such that, on unary input $1^n$, the machine halts while using
$O(s(n))$ tape cells and outputs the binary numeral $\operatorname{bin}(s(n))$.

On this page, whenever a constructible bound is used to clock another machine,
we also require the evident size condition
$$ n\le t(n) $$
for large enough $n$, so that the budget is at least large enough to read an
input of length $n$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field. On the vector space
$\mathcal B(X,Y)$ of bounded linear operators, the operator norm of
[[def-operator-norm]] is a norm.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For all vectors $x,y$ in a real or complex inner-product space,

$$|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\| ,$$

with equality if and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent.

derivations.claim: Detect source work-head collisions before decomposing a transition. The following classical marker construction stores positions without retaining their potentially long binary addresses. Logical cell $a$ on track $b$ is physical cell $Ka+b$. For every source work head $j$, keep one classical probe parked at $Ka_j+b_j$ and a single $1$ on marker track $j$ at logical position $a_j$; all other bits of that track are zero. Park the initially coincident physical heads at their distinct tracks using identity operations, then set the initial markers at logical zero. The origin track has its sole $1$ at zero and is never changed. To test $a_i=a_j$, move probe $i$ within its current stride block to marker track $j$, read its bit, and return to its parking track. Only that probe leaves its parking track during this test, so at the read no other classical head coincides with it. Transient collisions during movement perform identity operations only. Test all relevant pairs; there are only constantly many. Before a source movement clear each head's old marker using its own probe; then move the probes with their source heads and set their new markers before any further test. A local source move takes $K$ physical moves; probe the origin track to clamp a left move at logical zero. Duplicate each freshly emitted jump-address bit onto the probe's own erased index tape and append its fixed parking-label bits before use, obtaining $Ka_j+b_j$ without storing or rereading the address. Each source bit is duplicated only constantly many times. This maintains all markers exactly, costs constant time per source transition beyond charged index emission, uses fixed heads and alphabet, and has extent $O(s+1)$. Classical source symbols can likewise be read one probe at a time on the shared data track, saved in finite control, and written sequentially after evaluating the source's fixed classical function; the equality partition determines precisely whether that source operation is omitted. Auxiliary heads remain on distinct tracks, so source collisions do not suppress compiler or marker work. Apply the quantum source's collision-omission rule to the same equality partition: an omitted unitary is replaced by the empty word, not by its elementary factors. Otherwise its operands are distinct and are held fixed throughout its compiled block. The original quantum tape and its query blocks are not interleaved.

For a fixed machine, only finitely many local transition unitaries occur, each on a fixed number of qubits. For every nonomitted unitary in step 1.1, decompose it into a constant number of one-qubit gates and CNOTs using [A1], with polynomial-time Cauchy names for the resulting fixed one-qubit factors. Let $T\le c_Tt$ be the fixed-machine transition clock, with $c_T\ge1$, and let $c_M\ge1$ bound the one-qubit factors per transition. By [A2], compile each factor to projective error at most $1/(20c_Mc_Tt)$ as a word over $F=\operatorname{diag}(1,(3+4i)/5)$, its adjoint, and $H$; CNOT and query gates remain exact. Direct multiplication gives $F^*F=I$ because $(3-4i)(3+4i)=25$; [F3] gives unitary $H$ and CNOT, and [F1] gives the query basis permutation. The finite-bit compiler has word length, time and workspace polynomial in $\log t$, since the fixed-factor Cauchy procedures have polynomial query time and the requested tolerance has $O(\log t)$ bits. Execute its deterministic work sequentially while holding the original quantum operand heads stationary. Preserve the source's classical transition, fresh index-bit emissions and scheduled jumps/queries once; extra compiler cycles neither duplicate nor consume its pending index words. Use the interleaved classical data, probes and scratch tracks of step 1.1, keeping a snapshot of the source input/classical scanned symbols from the beginning of its transition. Fixed extra classical heads access the compiler scratch track sequentially, whose used length is $\mathrm{polylog}(t)$; the resulting classical extent is $O(s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$. The original quantum work tape, operand positions and quantum-query endpoint indices are unchanged, so every native quantum-query block remains contiguous as in [F1]. The constructible bounds [F4] clock these loops, giving compiled time $t'=O(t\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$ and work extent $O(s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t)$.

For a computational-basis measurement [F1], put $P_j=|j\rangle\langle j|$ for $j=0,1$; direct calculation gives $P_j^*=P_j$, $P_j^2=P_j$, $P_0P_1=0$, and $P_0+P_1=I$. The output branches are orthogonal by [F8]–[F9], and their squared norms sum to $\|\psi\|^2$ by the projector identities just checked. A transition with no measurement leaves that slot at $|00\rangle$. Thus every complete history has a fixed-length record string over the $T$ slots; distinct histories differ in some slot, so [F8]–[F9] make their record subspaces orthogonal, and subsequent classically controlled operations preserve orthogonality by [F1]. These record slots are not allocated by the simulator. A collision-omitted unitary has no compiled factors and zero approximation error. Projective compilation may multiply a one-qubit gate by a phase. Within each fixed history $h$ and transition time $r$, all one-qubit factors act on the same quantum state, so their phases multiply to one scalar $\lambda_{h,r}$ on that whole transition block. The direct sum over orthogonal history blocks has this same bound: for $v=\bigoplus_hv_h$ and block errors $E_h$, $\|(\bigoplus_hE_h)v\|^2=\sum_h\|E_hv_h\|^2\le(1/(20c_Tt))^2\sum_h\|v_h\|^2$. Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

Fix a length-$n$ finite promise computation from [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]], with input $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, zero-initialized auxiliary register $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$, circuit unitary $U_{C_n}$, and ordered output-wire tuple $O_n$. Let $P_{O_n}$ be the tensor-factor permutation that moves $O_n$, in its declared order, to the front, and let $W_n$ be the ordered tuple of all remaining wires ([[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]). Set
$$\psi_x:=U_{C_n}(|x\rangle\otimes|0^{a(n)}\rangle),\qquad v_x:=\operatorname{coord}(P_{O_n}\psi_x).$$
Here coordinates are in the ordered computational basis. In this definition, $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\rm root}:=\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\otimes}$ denotes the inner product on the reordered complete tensor register from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For $z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}$ and $w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}$, write $e_{z,w}$ for the corresponding product-basis vector and define
$$p_{C_n}(z\mid x):=\sum_{w\in\{0,1\}^{|W_n|}}\left|\langle P_{O_n}\psi_x,e_{z,w}\rangle_{\rm root}\right|^2.$$
The acceptance probability is
$$p_{C_n}(x):=\sum_{\substack{z\in\{0,1\}^{|O_n|}\\A_n(x,z)=1}}p_{C_n}(z\mid x).$$
Equivalently, if $E_{A,x}$ is the diagonal projection onto the basis vectors $(z,w)$ with $A_n(x,z)=1$, then $p_{C_n}(x)=\operatorname{Tr}(E_{A,x}v_xv_x^\dagger)$; the matrix adjoint is conjugate transpose in an orthonormal basis ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]]).

These are finite sums. The definition itself does not assert normalization, positivity of the resulting operator expression, or a probability bound; those consequences are the purpose of [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]]. No Dirac bra convention is used here: every amplitude uses the root pairing displayed above.

A promise problem $\Pi=(Y,N)$ belongs to **BQP in the QC14 model** when there exist a full-list uniform family $(C_n)$ and a polynomial-time acceptance predicate $A_n$ as in [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]] and [[def-qc-quantum-acceptance-probability]] such that, for every $x\in Y$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\ge\frac23,$$
and for every $x\in N$,
$$p_{C_{|x|}}(x)\le\frac13.$$
By [[thm-qc-output-acceptance-law-normalizes]], $p_{C_n}(x)$ is the probability of the specified acceptance event and lies in $[0,1]$. No condition is imposed for $x\notin Y\cup N$ ([[def-promise-problem]]). The gate alphabet is exactly $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$; its matrix entries lie in $\mathbb Q(\zeta_8)=\mathbb Q(i,\sqrt2)$ as specified by [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]. This definition does not assert a BQP-versus-classical separation, nor does it assert an unproved equivalence with another circuit-uniformity convention.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call. Inverse availability and query or gate charges are also recorded separately from controlled forward access. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

For sufficiently constructible $t,s\ge\log n$, the published VMW model with charged operand extent satisfies
$$\mathrm{BQTISP}(t,s)\subseteq\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\rm basis}(t\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t,s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t).$$
The output uses the derived classical basis profile in [[def-qc-unbounded-error-time-space-counting-model]], with a fixed finite number of separate binary work tapes and native basis input queries. All work cells addressed by local operations or a query, including the highest query endpoint, count toward work extent. This is the explicit operand-space formalization of the published model; no general conversion to the erased-index head-access-only or sequential profile is asserted.

For either fixed profile $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, every real $d$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $c>1$ such that at least one of the following holds: $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}\notin\mathrm{PrTIME}_{P}(n^c)$, or $\mathrm{MajSAT}\notin\mathrm{PrTISP}_{P}(n^d,n^{1-\varepsilon})$. The basis profile is the derived full-basis comparison model. Formula thresholds are at least-half and machine acceptance is strict majority.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. There are only finitely many scalars in a fixed finite expression tree, so for its nonzero divisors some integer $B$ has $|z|\ge2^{-B}$ throughout; $B$ may be hardcoded. A fixed zero is returned as zero. Nonnegative roots are allowed even at zero, and nested roots only multiply the requested precision by a fixed constant at each of finitely many levels. Thus the finite compositions still use polynomial time in $p+1$. Conjugation merely changes an imaginary sign.

The path instruction in [F3] is an exact factorization. Each prescribed pattern-controlled $X$ exchanges precisely the adjacent path labels $g_j,g_{j+1}$ and fixes every other computational-basis label, because its $n-1$ controls must match the common bits. Let $P$ be the permutation effected by the swaps in their stated order. Then $P(x)=g_{d-1}$ and $P(y)=y=g_d$. The middle block, with the stated block reversal when the target bit of $g_{d-1}$ is $1$, acts by $V$ on the ordered pair $(g_{d-1},g_d)$ and fixes its complement. The complete chronological list therefore has matrix $P^*MP$, where $M$ is that middle block. Since $P$ is a permutation and maps $x,y$ to the selected pair, no other basis label maps into that pair; the conjugate acts by $V$ on $(x,y)$ and fixes every other basis vector. The controlled-gate expansions are exact by [F4] and [F5], and the negative-control conjugations retain their exact matrices. Thus every two-level factor used here is exactly the one specified by [F3], including its scalar phase.

A square root of any fixed polynomial-Cauchy unit scalar $u$ can also be selected polynomially. Choose a fixed $\zeta\in\{1,-1,i,-i\}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(\zeta u)\ge1/2$; such a choice exists because the larger absolute coordinate of a unit complex number is at least $1/\sqrt2$. Put $v=\zeta u$ and $a=\sqrt{(1+\operatorname{Re}v)/2}$, $b=\operatorname{Im}v/(2a)$. Then $a\ge\sqrt3/2$ and $(a+ib)^2=v$. Multiply by either fixed algebraic square root of $\zeta^{-1}$ and choose its fixed sign to obtain either desired root of $u$. Step 1.1 applies with a positive constant denominator. Iterating gives any fixed finite tower of coherently chosen phase half-roots. A root of a fixed nonzero complex scalar $z$ is obtained by first normalizing $z/|z|$ and multiplying its unit root by $\sqrt{|z|}$; the zero case is hardcoded separately.

For each $U\in\mathcal U$, run the finite algebraic Givens construction [F2] as a mathematical factorization. Hardcode its actual finite skip decisions $b=0$; no run-time zero test on a varying Cauchy name is required. In each unskipped operation $h>0$ is a fixed constant, so all entries of that Givens matrix and the updated matrix are polynomial-Cauchy by step 1.1. There are at most $2^k(2^k-1)/2$ operations, a constant. The terminal diagonal entries and the exact two-level adjoints therefore have polynomial-Cauchy entries. A phase on one chosen computational word is a pattern-controlled $\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda)$ or $\operatorname{diag}(\lambda,1)$ on a selected wire, with the other wires matching that word; hence the terminal diagonal is a fixed finite product of pattern-controlled one-qubit matrices of the same effective class.

The square roots required by [F4] preserve this effective class. For a fixed two-dimensional unitary $W$, if $W=\lambda I$ choose a unit root $\mu$ by step 2.1 and take $\mu I$. Otherwise the spectral theorem [F6] gives two distinct eigenvalues. The nonzero discriminant $d_0=(\operatorname{tr}W)^2-4\det W$ has a root $d$ as in step 2.1, and $\lambda_\pm=(\operatorname{tr}W\pm d)/2$ have modulus one. The projector $P_+=(W-\lambda_-I)/(\lambda_+-\lambda_-)$ and $P_-=I-P_+$ are orthogonal by [F6]. Choose unit roots $\mu_\pm$ and put $V=\mu_+P_++\mu_-P_-$. Then $V$ is unitary, $V^2=W$, and every entry is polynomial-Cauchy by step 1.1 and step 2.1. The scalar/nonscalar branch and the positive eigenvalue-gap lower bound are fixed choices, not input-dependent equality decisions.

The constant one-control construction [F5] is effective as well. Choose a unit root $\lambda$ of $\det W$ by step 2.1 and normalize $S=\lambda^{-1}W\in SU(2)$. Write $S=\begin{pmatrix}a&-\overline c\\c&\overline a\end{pmatrix}$ and $\rho=|a|$, $\sigma=|c|$. If $\rho>0$ use $a/\rho$ for its phase, otherwise fix its arbitrary phase to $1$; treat $c/\sigma$ the same way. Choose fixed real arguments $\gamma,\eta$ with $a=e^{-i\gamma}\rho$ and $c=e^{i\eta}\sigma$, and choose $0\le\theta\le\pi$ with $\cos(\theta/2)=\rho$, $\sin(\theta/2)=\sigma$. These are only notation: the algorithm never computes their real arguments. Every matrix entry of the Euler factors and of $A,B,C$ in [F5] is a finite sum or product of the unit phases and their coherently selected half-roots, together with $\rho,\sigma$, $\sqrt{(1+\rho)/2}$ and $\sqrt{(1-\rho)/2}$. Indeed the latter are $\cos(\theta/4),\sin(\theta/4)$; the z-rotation entries are exponentials of half-angles of $\alpha=\gamma+\eta$ and $\beta=\gamma-\eta$, hence phase roots from step 2.1. Choose their fixed signs to match these displayed arguments. Thus all four arbitrary one-qubit matrices in the exact controlled construction are polynomial-Cauchy; their multiplication retains the control phase $\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda)$ exactly. No numerical angle oracle is assumed.

Apply the Gray-path implementation [F3] to each two-level block from step 2.2, and apply the no-workspace recursion [F4] to its pattern-controlled gates and to the diagonal phase gates. Negative controls and permutation gates have fixed algebraic entries. Each root step stays in the effective class by step 3.1 and each controlled base case does so by step 3.2. Exact factorization follows from step 1.2 and step 3.1 and step 3.2 and [F2]–[F5], including each scalar phase; the resulting gate factors and lengths have precisely the asserted properties.

Fix the explicit complete transition-table coding specified below. There are two distinct fixed finite-alphabet probabilistic interpreters, one for the sequential access profile and one for the erased-index head-access-only random-access profile. Each interpreter simulates valid descriptions $e$ with input $x$ and an external binary clock $b$, reproducing exactly the source acceptance or rejection reached in at most $b$ source transitions and rejecting nonhalting expiry. The simulated fair-bit distribution is exact. Writing $n=|x|$ and $L=|e|+1$, there are absolute constants $C,d$ such that each simulation takes time
$$ C L^d\bigl(n+(b+1)\log^d(n+b+L+2)\bigr). $$
For the index-only profile, jump addresses are written on one-way sequential write-only index tapes erased after use; the older nonerasing delimited-head profile is a distinct profile and is not covered by this index-only assertion. The fixed interpreter has a fixed finite physical head count even when the described source head count varies. Malformed descriptions halt rejecting. This is a time simulation; no preservation of the source's simultaneous space bound is asserted.

In particular, for each fixed polynomially bounded time-constructible $T(n)\ge n$ and fixed $c$, descriptions of length at most $c\log(n+2)$ are simulated in either one fixed declared profile in $O(T(n)\,\mathrm{polylog}(n+2))$ time, including the clock constructor. Arbitrary superpolynomial clocks retain the general displayed bound rather than this specialization.

Use fixed finite-control fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only binary input followed by blanks and a fixed finite number of work tapes and heads, with a finite explicit transition-table code. Each nonhalting transition consumes one independent fair bit as in [[def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface]]. Fix one access profile for each complexity class.

In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. The clocked-normalization lemma proves the required time-only simulation into that profile for clocks at least the input length; no general sublinear-time equivalence is asserted.

For historical comparison, the **preprint-delimited VMW profile** retains the 2007 preprint convention: a jump reads the address written between two classical work-tape heads, without the final paper's write-only erased index tapes. This is a separately named profile. No equivalence or preservation of time/space bounds between the preprint-delimited and published profiles is asserted. Results proved below for the published profile do not establish their extension to the preprint-delimited profile.

Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. For a fixed profile, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(t)$ uses strict acceptance probability greater than $1/2$ on members and at most $1/2$ on nonmembers; $\mathrm{PrTISP}(t,s)$ adds the stated space bound. Subscripts $\mathrm{seq}$, $\mathrm{index}$, $\mathrm{basis}$, and $\mathrm{preprint}$ distinguish the four profiles. An exact classical oracle is deterministic; writing its queries and returning from them are charged, and total query-string length is at most the outer running time.

For either $P\in\{\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{basis}\}$, define $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)$ and $\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j+1}=\mathrm{PrTIME}_P(n)^{\mathrm{LCH}_{P,j}}$. Oracle queries are exact and all fair-bit branches belong to the outer machine. An omitted profile in an item must be fixed explicitly by that item's hypotheses; profiles are never silently identified.

A $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ formula has a fixed finite set of Boolean variables and is accepted when at least half of assignments satisfy it. A $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ formula has two disjoint ordered variable blocks and is accepted when at least half of outer assignments leave a residual formula true on at least half of inner assignments. Use a common explicit plain-formula encoding for MajSAT. MajMajSAT accepts this same plain encoding with one implicit fresh unused outer variable and all formula variables in the inner block; it also accepts a separately tagged encoding with the two variable blocks explicitly listed. Thus every plain MajSAT instance embeds identically, bit for bit, into MajMajSAT with unchanged truth value. The unused outer variable is part of the decoded fixed finite variable set. Concretely, use distinct fixed tags for plain and partitioned inputs, a unary declaration of the number of variables, fixed-width variable indices, and prefix-encoded binary AND/OR and unary NOT gates (with constant tokens). The partitioned form also gives the outer-block split; variables are renamed into block order. Plain-format validity is checked by one pending-subexpression counter, variable-range checks and a scan of the declared fields, using $O(n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$ time and $O(\log n)$ workspace. These conventions do not alter either at-least-half threshold. Malformed encodings are rejected by both problems.

derivations.claim: First construct and justify the only balancing procedure used below. An insertion-only AVL tree is a binary search tree with each node storing its key, two child pointers, a parent pointer, height, subtree size and optional OR aggregate. Set the height of an empty subtree to zero. Maintain that the two child heights differ by at most one. A tree of height $h$ has at least $N_h$ nodes, where $N_0=0$, $N_1=1$ and $N_h\ge1+N_{h-1}+N_{h-2}$. For $h\ge2$ this implies $N_h+1\ge2(N_{h-2}+1)$, since the minimum sizes are nondecreasing. Induction therefore gives $N_h+1\ge2^{\lfloor h/2\rfloor}$, so $h\le2\log_2(N_h+1)+1$. Consequently the invariant implies logarithmic root-to-node paths, without any distributional assumption on keys.

Search by the ordinary ordered comparisons. An absent key is inserted as a leaf at the null child where search ends. Retrace its ancestor path, recomputing height, subtree size, and OR aggregate from each node's two children and its own value. Until the first unbalanced ancestor, each subtree height increases by at most one; these metadata updates are required whether or not a rotation occurs. If no ancestor is unbalanced, the height invariant already holds. Otherwise let $z$ be the lowest unbalanced ancestor. Suppose its left height has become two greater than its right height; the opposite case is the left/right reflection. Let $y$ be its left child. The child $y$ cannot have equal child heights: if its new child heights were $t,t$, one child would be unchanged at $t$, so its old maximum child height would already have been $t$ and its own height would not have increased. Thus the new child heights of $y$ differ by one. If $y$ is left-heavy, write the heights of its left subtree, its right subtree and $z$'s right subtree as $t+1,t,t$. Rotate right at $z$, making $y$ the root of this local subtree. Its right child is now $z$, whose two child heights are $t,t$, hence whose height is $t+1$; $y$'s two child heights are both $t+1$, hence its height is $t+2$. Recompute the fields of the rotated nodes bottom-up, then continue the metadata updates above the repaired subtree. All local balances are valid. The old pre-insertion subtree at $z$ also had height $t+2$, so this restores that old height. [step 1.1, construct]

In the remaining left-heavy case, $y$ is right-heavy. Let $w$ be $y$'s right child. Write the heights of $y$'s left subtree and $z$'s right subtree as $t,t$. The two child subtrees of $w$ have heights each at most $t$, at least $t-1$ when nonempty as required by AVL balance, and maximum $t$. Rotate left at $y$, then right at $z$, making $w$ the local root. Its left child $y$ now has child heights $t$ and at most $t$ differing by at most one, hence height $t+1$; its right child $z$ has the analogous heights and also height $t+1$. The root $w$ has height $t+2$, again the old pre-insertion height at $z$. This also covers $t=0$, where the relevant empty children have height zero. The right-heavy cases are exact reflections. Rotations preserve the in-order key sequence: the single rotation changes $((A,y,B),z,C)$ to $(A,y,(B,z,C))$, and the double rotation changes $((A,y,(B,w,C)),z,D)$ to $((A,y,B),w,(C,z,D))$. All nodes retain their stable identities, while a constant number of child/parent pointers change. After this first repair the subtree's old height is restored, so higher ancestors cannot acquire a new imbalance. Recompute height, size and OR first on the lower rotated nodes, then their new root, and then along the remaining ancestor path. Thus search and insertion use $O(\log(N+2))$ node operations, and maintain all stated fields. This proves the needed AVL result locally; no deletions will be used.

For each virtual binary work tape keep an **outer** insertion-only AVL tree whose keys are canonical numerical block prefixes $P$ in the representation $a=PB+r$, $0\le r<B$. Each outer node has a permanent compact block ID equal to its stable allocation ID. Store a canonical binary prefix word and its length at that node. To compare a freshly supplied prefix of length $A'$ with a stored prefix, first compare their lengths, which are short integers. If unequal this decides numerical order; if equal compare their $A'$ bits lexicographically. Each comparison costs $O(A'+\log H+\log L)$ elementary short-address/bit operations, including access to the stored key. Search/insertion makes $O(\log(N+2))$ such comparisons by step 1.1 and step 2.1 and step 3.1. Only head-jump or query-endpoint registration requires such a fresh-key search. As in [F1], on every registration also register $P-1$ if nonnegative and $P+1$, whose canonical words can be formed by ordinary scans in $O(A'+1)$ work. The sum of all these key lengths is $L^{O(1)}(b+1)$ by fresh-index charging in [F1]; duplicate keys are not stored twice. This bounds all long-prefix reading and key comparison costs by $L^{O(1)}(b+1)\mathrm{polylog}\,H$. Initial prefix zero and its neighbor one add only fixed keys per virtual tape.

Every outer node owns an **inner** insertion-only AVL tree of all offsets so far accessed in that block. Its keys are $s$-bit offsets; its node stores the current binary cell value. Keep nodes even when their value becomes zero, so deletion is unnecessary. The inner subtree OR is the OR of its nodes' cell values. The outer node's own OR is its inner root's OR, or zero for an empty inner tree; its subtree OR combines its own OR and the two outer child subtree ORs. A new cell is initially zero, and then receives any prescribed write. Each source local operation accesses only $L^{O(1)}$ cells. A query will access at most $k+1$ individual cells in addition to its range-OR operation below. Hence the number of inner nodes is at most $L^{O(1)}(b+1)(k+1)$. Searching/inserting an offset costs $O(\log(N+2))$ comparisons of $s$-bit keys. A bit-value change recomputes OR along its inner ancestor path and then along its owning outer node's ancestor path; rotations maintain the same aggregates by step 3.1. Thus one short-offset access/write costs $L^{O(1)}\mathrm{polylog}\,H$ physical work. Unregistered prefixes and absent offsets represent zero cells.

The parent pointers and subtree sizes allow numerical comparisons of **already registered** block IDs without rereading their possibly long keys. Compute the in-order rank of a known node $v$ as its left-subtree size plus one, then ascend to the root, adding one plus the ancestor's left-subtree size whenever the current node is that ancestor's right child. Every node visited contributes exactly the keys preceding $v$ that lie in the corresponding ancestor piece, so the result is the exact one-based numerical rank. This uses $O(\log(N+2))$ short-record operations by step 1.1. Stable node IDs and current parent/size fields remain valid after rotations. No insertion occurs while the ranks of one operation are being used. Two compact cell addresses are compared by these outer ranks and then their short offsets. Local head moves use the same three cached adjacent-prefix IDs as [F1]: between source jumps a head travels at most $b<B$ cells, so cannot leave those three blocks. In particular repeated crossings of a block boundary cost only short-offset arithmetic and cached-ID selection. They never incur another long-prefix comparison.

Prove the range-OR procedure explicitly. In an AVL tree whose nodes have in-order ranks, sizes and OR aggregates, the OR of a contiguous rank interval is obtainable in $O(\log(N+2))$ node visits. At a subtree, its root rank and child rank intervals are computed from a carried starting rank and the left size. If a subtree's whole rank interval is inside the query interval, use its stored aggregate; if disjoint, skip it; otherwise recurse on the intersecting children and include the root's own value if its rank is in the interval. At each depth only subtrees containing one of the two query boundaries can require recursion: at most two partially intersected subtrees, together with at most a constant number of their fully included/disjoint children. Thus total visits are $O(\text{height}+1)$. Inner offset trees use ordinary $s$-bit key comparisons to locate offset bounds, with the same procedure or the corresponding two boundary paths. For a source address interval $[a,c)$, if both endpoints have the same block ID, query that inner offset interval. If their block IDs differ, OR the suffix of the left inner tree, the prefix of the right inner tree, and the outer subtree range strictly between their numerical ranks. Registered endpoint prefixes exist by registration, even if their inner trees are empty. All untouched cells contribute zero. This computes exactly the OR of every source work bit in $[a,c)$, including arbitrarily large gaps of unvisited zero cells, in $L^{O(1)}\mathrm{polylog}\,H$ work.

Realize the data structures in the index-only target by the fixed physical protocol in [F1]. Source index words occupy separate $b+1$-cell reserved regions; arithmetic reservation does not scan them. Store the long prefix words in append-allocated arrays. Allocate each outer/inner node as a fixed-width binary record with short child/parent pointers, height/size, current bit or inner-root pointer, and OR fields. The outer-node count and total long-key length are $L^{O(1)}(b+1)$; the inner-node count is $L^{O(1)}(b+1)\log H$. All record lengths are $L^{O(1)}\log H$, so the largest physical address is $L^{O(1)}(b+1)\log^{O(1)}H$. Select a padded pointer width $q=K(s+\lceil\log_2 L\rceil+1)$ for a sufficiently large absolute $K$; the preceding bound is smaller than $2^q$. Every pointer, height, size and low-offset arithmetic operand fits in polynomially many $q$-bit fields. A constant number of fixed physical heads, reserved scratch regions, emitted short erased input/work indices and ordinary local scans implements each elementary node or array-bit operation in $L^{O(1)}\mathrm{polylog}\,H$ transitions, as in [F1]. No extra physical head per source head, arbitrary alphabet extension, unit-cost large-integer operation, or long uncharged address is used.

On a source basis query, consume and register the two fresh endpoint index words, with their neighboring prefixes, as in step 4.1. Save the answer bit at address $v$. Starting from endpoint $v$, take at most $k$ virtual predecessor steps, stopping at $u$. Each predecessor uses only short-offset arithmetic and the cached three-prefix neighborhood of $v$, because $k\le b<B$ for $n\ge1$; when $n=0$, $k=0$ and no predecessor step is needed. Record the encountered bits, in reverse order, to obtain the last $\min(k,v-u)$ address bits. Comparisons with $u$ use compact ranks/offsets from step 5.2, not long key strings. Let $p$ be the position reached, namely $\max(u,v-k)$. Query range-OR on $[u,p)$ using step 6.1. If that OR is one, some address bit more significant than the last $k$ bits is nonzero, so the query address is at least $2^k>n$ and the answer must stay unchanged. If it is zero, the entire numerical input address is the recorded low word, padded with leading zeros to $k$ bits. Compare that short integer $i$ with $1$ and $n$. Outside $1\le i\le n$, leave the answer unchanged; inside this range, emit the physical input address for bit $i$ (subtract one, then add any fixed paired-input encoding offset) on the index-only target's ordinary input index tape, make the native classical input read, and XOR the retrieved input bit into the saved answer cell. In the empty-address case $u=v$, the low word is zero and $x_0=0$ as specified. This exactly implements $Q_x$ on all basis work configurations, while never invoking a block query in the target. The source address register can be reused indefinitely; each operation uses aggregates and short accesses rather than rescanning that register.

The charged long-prefix operations total $L^{O(1)}(b+1)\mathrm{polylog}\,H$ by step 4.1. Each source transition additionally uses $L^{O(1)}\mathrm{polylog}\,H$ for finite-table lookup, short head updates, collisions, ordinary cell reads/writes, and at most one fixed finite number of basis queries. A basis query contributes at most $k=O(\log(b+2))$ short cell accesses, a constant number of rank/range-OR operations, and a short emitted input index, all bounded by the same type of polylogarithmic factor. Multiply by the short-record physical cost from step 6.2, add the $O(n)$ input-length scan and polynomial code initialization, and enlarge the absolute exponent $d$ to obtain the theorem's bound. The same allocation bound proves the asserted time-scale maximum address. This is solely a time normalization; the dictionary need not respect a smaller original source space bound.

Use [F1]'s external-clock driver: test halting before expiry, consume one designated fresh fair bit for the next source table, save the complete source instructions, and apply their operations with the source's simultaneous-action and collision conventions. Ordinary source operations are exact by [F1] and the compact numerical address/value invariants; a source block query is exact by step 7.1. Induction reproduces the entire source basis configuration after each simulated transition. All added dictionary, balancing, rank, OR and input-read work is deterministic. Ignoring physical fair bits except the designated source choices therefore preserves every consumed source prefix's probability $2^{-j}$; summing disjoint terminal prefixes preserves acceptance, rejection and timeout probabilities exactly. A halt on transition $b$ is reported, and nonhalting expiry rejects.

For descriptions of length $O(\log(n+2))$ and fixed polynomially bounded clocks $b=T(n)\ge n$, both $L$ and $\log H$ are polylogarithmic in $n+2$, so step 8.1 gives $O(T(n)\,\mathrm{polylog}(n+2))$ time. A fixed deterministic clock constructor can first be simulated by the already proved index-only external-clock interpreter with doubling budgets, as in the combined clocked candidate, with total time $O(T(n)\,\mathrm{polylog}(n+2))$. The resulting index-only target is included in the basis-query profile. Thus the time-hierarchy diagonal can use this normalized interpreter in the basis-query profile, and Cook-style trace encodings can use its bounded-address index-only computation. In the **sequential** profile, heads move locally by at most one cell per transition. In the **erased-index head-access** profile, use the head-access mechanism of the final 2012 Van Melkebeek–Watson model: a zero-initialized binary classical work tape, a fixed finite number of input/work heads, and classical finite control. Each head may move left, right, stay, or jump in one transition to an address computed on a designated one-way sequential-access write-only index tape. Index tapes are initially empty, writing each bit is charged to the ordinary transition count, and an index tape is erased after each use. The original input tape is read-only and contains the input followed by blanks. If coincident work heads make an operation undefined, omit that work-tape operation in the transition. All heads start at the left boundary; left motion there clamps at zero.

The **published VMW derived basis restriction**, denoted the **basis** profile, also permits the classical basis action of the source's native coherent input query. On a contiguous block $[l,r]$ of a specified binary work tape, the first $r-l$ bits give the binary input index $i$ in most-significant-first order and the last cell holds $b$; the query replaces only $b$ by $b\mathbin\oplus x_i$, using zero on invalid input indices. Both endpoints are freshly emitted on erased index tapes. The native query costs one transition, as in the published quantum model. The input indices are $1,\ldots,n$, with $x_0=0$; the empty address word denotes zero, and reversed endpoints cause omission of the query. Allow a fixed finite number of binary work tapes, local operations of fixed finite arity, and native queries on any specified tape: this is the fixed finite product of these classical basis operations, permitting separate path-simulation rows. This is an explicit locally defined comparison model derived from the quantum operations. The source does not separately state a formal classical block-query machine definition, and no equivalence with the index-only profile is assumed. Time is the maximum number of transitions on every branch. Sequential space counts distinct visited work cells. Erased-index and basis space use the maximum address of every work cell accessed on any branch, including the highest endpoint of every native basis-query block; read-only input and index tapes are not counted in this maximum-address measure. The preprint-delimited space convention is likewise its maximum visited work-head address. Its odd fan-in is $2D+1$, so under either convention for majority it tests $S_q+(D-h+1)\ge D+1$, equivalently $S_q\ge h$. Write this output as $T_{q,h}$ and set $T_{q,0}=1$, $T_{q,D+1}=0$.
